analysis:
The PR's only substantive change to docs/architecture/inference.md is a date bump at line 3 and a new section at head lines 4816-4826, titled 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers'. It documents that GPT-OSS plain decode steps commit a Metal command buffer every 100 operations, with no input-size bound. This goes through `GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers` and `CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding`, and prefill keeps MLX defaults. It claims results do not depend on the partitioning. The supplied units (base lines 3235-4002) are unchanged surrounding text, and the changed section itself is not visible in them. It appears only in the patch excerpt.

Security relevance is limited to TB-007 (inference engine) and T-029 (GPU resource monopolisation). The change is a performance tuning of GPU command-buffer commit cadence and touches no keys, attestation, coordinator protocol, encryption or prefix-cache storage. The documentation does not alter T-041 (prefix cache), the HMAC lookup tags, the TTL or the KEK handling, and it does not change any trust boundary. The claim that results are partition-independent is a correctness claim, not a security control. The underlying Swift source change (`GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers`) is not in this batch, so I cannot verify that raising the per-buffer operation limit does not affect memory pressure, the in-flight command buffer limit, or cancellation latency (T-010). That is an integration question for any pass that sees the code.

The surrounding unchanged docs on Flint, cluster probes and tensor-parallel history files were read only for context. They mention owner-only local files and cluster state, and they raise no new regression from this PR. I found no security regression.
